relationships.description: The field-level masking rule applies only when the access condition's request-context test holds, so the condition decides at runtime whether the field is shown in clear or masked.
relationships.evidence: The field masking configuration or policy file lists a condition (e.g. subject.department == resource.owner_department) that the masking interceptor evaluates before choosing clear or masked output for that field.

relationships.description: The sensitivity tier assigned to the protected field sets the minimum masking, hashing or tokenization strength that the field-level rule must apply.
relationships.evidence: The schema or data catalog tags the column with a classification label (e.g. PII/Confidential), and the field's masking rule references that label or meets the protection obligation the label declares.

relationships.description: The field-level rule dictates how one named field of the protected resource must be presented to unprivileged principals, setting handling rules the resource's data exposure must follow.
relationships.evidence: The resource's access-control definition or entity annotations (e.g. @Masked on a model property, a column masking policy on a table) attach the field rule to a named field of that resource.

relationships.description: The field masking rule is the concrete field-level enforcement of a policy rule's permit/deny decision, turning a deny into redaction of the field's value instead of refusing the whole request.
relationships.evidence: The policy definition (e.g. an OPA/Rego rule or XACML rule) is referenced by ID from the field masking configuration, or the serializer's masking code branches on that rule's evaluated effect.

relationships.description: The field-level rule shields the sensitive value of one field of the protected resource from disclosure to principals who lack clear-text access.
relationships.evidence: API responses or query results for the resource show the named field masked, hashed or truncated for an unprivileged test principal, driven by the masking rule bound to that field.

relationships.description: The field is revealed in clear only to principals who hold the named permission, and everyone else receives the masked, redacted or tokenized form.
relationships.evidence: The masking rule declares an unmask permission (e.g. 'customer.ssn:read-clear'), and the enforcement code checks that permission on the caller before skipping the masking step.

notes: governs and protects toward SecureResource overlap. Both describe the field rule acting on the resource's field. Consider keeping only protects. Also, SecureResource is described as owning its FieldAccessControls, so a composition from the resource side would be more accurate than governs.
